root_causes.description: The frontend is the only service showing anomalous behavior in the window: its server error rate is non-zero (peaking ~0.019/s) while every downstream service (checkout, payment, cart, shipping, currency, product-catalog, recommendation, ad, email) reports 0.000/s, and its p99 server latency is pinned at a flat 10000ms. Frontend traces (user_browse_product) run ~15s with a window p95 of ~75s, indicating the frontend request path is stalling, which produces the client-facing error rate that triggered the watchdog alert.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate max=0.019, p99=0.018, mean=0.003 (only non-zero service; all other services 0.000)
frontend span user_browse_product duration=15002ms; window p95_duration=75024ms over 20 traces, 0 flagged as errors

root_causes.description: Frontend server error rate is non-zero and anomalous relative to a 0 baseline, consistent with aborted or timed-out requests driving the HighClientErrorRate alert. Error traces were not surfaced (0 of 20), so this is a weaker secondary hypothesis than the dominant latency signal.

evidence.observed_value: error_rate spiked to 0.019/s during the window

evidence.expected_baseline: no error traces and p95 duration < 1000ms

evidence.observed_value: [no logs found] in the incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: no error log lines expected in steady state

root_causes.description: Checkout fans out to cart, payment, email, shipping, currency and product-catalog, and a slow or failing downstream could stall the frontend browse/checkout path. However checkout itself showed error_rate=0.000 and stable CPU (~0.028 cores), and it was not confirmed by traces or logs, so this remains a low-confidence alternative.

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage mean=0.028 cores, stable (no CPU stress)

remediation_steps: Inspect the frontend deployment for the injected latency/timeout condition (raised response delay or aborted request fault) and roll back the last config or flag change affecting the frontend request path.

Trace a slow user_browse_product request (e.g. trace e08029cd7d28db48) end-to-end to confirm whether the 10-15s stall originates inside frontend or in a downstream dependency (checkout, cart, payment, shipping, currency, product-catalog).
Temporarily raise frontend request timeouts and enable retries/pod autoscaling to absorb the stall while the fault is remediated.
Validate flagd feature flags for frontend-related fault injection, since flag-driven faults in the OTel demo can introduce latency or aborts at runtime.
Add a p99 latency alert on the frontend server span (threshold e.g. 1000ms) to catch the latency precursor that precedes the client error-rate alert.
